lawRefs: HB 463 (2025-2026 Reg. Sess.), signed May 11 2026, applicable to taxable years beginning on or after Jan 1 2026
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rate: HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026) cut the flat rate from 5.19% to 4.99% for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 (Tax Foundation's February 2026 table shows the superseded 5.19%). Further cuts of 0.125 points per year from 2027 toward 3.99% are subject to revenue triggers. Standard deduction for 2026 (HB 463): $30,000 married filing jointly; $15,000 single, head of household and married filing separately (scheduled to rise $750 / $375 a year from 2027 to $36,000 / $18,000, subject to the same trigger delays - these are scheduled steps, not inflation indexing). No additional standard deduction for age or blindness and no taxpayer/spouse personal exemption; the dependent exemption is $5,000 per dependent for 2026 (rising $125 a year from 2027 to $6,000) - not expressible in this schema. Starts from federal AGI. Social Security is fully excluded. Retirement income exclusion per person: $35,000 at age 62-64 (or permanently disabled), $65,000 at 65 and older (rises to $70,000 for 65+ from 2027); it covers pensions, annuities and investment income plus a limited amount of earned income. HB 463 also excludes up to $1,750 each of qualified overtime and cash tips for a limited period beginning 2026. No capital-gains exclusion.
